title: Working on content creation platform with focus on style consistency
author: rbetik12
selftext:
I started working on a casual mobile game for myself and quickly realized that making and drawing art assets at the early prototype stage was a bit too much for me.

At first, I just wanted to generate a mascot character and some basic assets for the game. It was something between a match-3 and merge-2 mobile game. While experimenting, I noticed how good current AI generation models have become. But I also noticed one important thing: using a single model is usually not enough to get a really decent result. You often need a combination of multiple models, kind of like in ComfyUI workflows.

The problem is that ComfyUI can feel pretty overwhelming for people who are not deep into AI content generation. So I decided to build a simpler tool for myself, and now I’d really like to gather some feedback on it.

Right now it supports:

* generating game assets
* editing generated assets
* animating assets (with exporting game engine ready spritesheet)
* generating voiceovers with configurable voices, so you can quickly add prototype voice lines to a game

One thing I tried to focus on is preserving the visual style of generated images. The idea is that you can create a reference style and reuse it across a project, instead of getting random-looking assets every time.

I’m also a big fan of board games, so I tried generating a character inspired by cozy woodland board game style, and the result was honestly pretty nice. [LINK](https://imgur.com/a/pe6s10p)

I am planning to add more cheaper generation using new models that make generation really cheap.

I am really open for feedback to help generating prototype assets or even game-ready assets for new games.

URL: [https://game-canvas.com/](https://game-canvas.com/)

comments.author: DaedalusRaistlin
comments.body:
I'm working in something similar myself. Different focus though, mine is aiming at 2D artwork to 3D models. Similar idea on how to get consistency, based on my own workflows. 

My main project is just getting too large, and I keep generating images and models I've already done before. 

Best of luck with your app and games! I think the big players in this space are moving fairly slowly with making nice workflows like this, so it's a good time to try to get in on it and make a service that stands out.
